title: AutoNTT: Automatic Architecture Design and Exploration for Number Theoretic Transform Acceleration on FPGAs
problem: NTT is a major computational bottleneck in FHE systems, but there lacks a systematic design automation tool to explore various NTT accelerator architectures that support diverse FHE parameters such as different polynomial sizes, modulo sizes, and reduction methods.
motivation: FHE is orders-of-magnitude slower than plain computation; addressing NTT bottlenecks through automated design is critical for practical FHE deployment.
method: AutoNTT is a tool that automatically designs hardware accelerators for NTT (a computational building block in cryptography) by converting high-level code into hardware designs (high-level synthesis). It explores three circuit arrangements—sequential processing (iterative), parallel pipeline processing (dataflow), and mixed approaches (hybrid)—across different polynomial sizes (2^10 to 2^17 elements) and number ranges (28-64 bits). The designs are optimized by reducing memory for temporary values and precomputed factors (twiddle factors), and by simplifying how the circuit's computation modules (butterfly units) connect.
key_novelty: The key innovation is automating the generation and exploration of multiple NTT accelerator architecture patterns to support diverse fully homomorphic encryption parameter ranges.
contributions: Automatic generation of multiple optimized NTT accelerator architectures (iterative, dataflow, hybrid) in HLS
Support for diverse FHE parameters: polynomial sizes 2^10-2^17 and modulo sizes 28-64 bits
Multiple reduction method support with architectural optimizations for buffer and interconnection efficiency
2.48× better latency and 3.61× better throughput versus prior work

metrics.other: similar FPGA resource utilization as prior work

primary_theme: Automatic design automation for NTT acceleration
